newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says Ok Tedi copper still in drought.
newsitem.headline: BHP says Ok Tedi copper still in drought.

text.p: The Ok Tedi copper mine in Papua New Guinea remained in the grips of drought on Friday, still unable to ship concentrates along the Fly River, a spokesman for the mine's operator, the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Friday.
"There is no change in the weather pattern," BHP public affairs adviser Yehiura Hriehwazi told Reuters by telephone from Port Moresby.
Hriehwazi insisted there would be no declaration of force majeure soon, despite delays to at least one freight load of concentrates to Japan so far and the prospect of additional delays.
"Force majeure is not enforceable in the foreseeable future because anything can happen, the situation can change suddenly overnight," he said.
He said Ok Tedi was maintaining a "constant dialogue" with its customers, mostly smelting companies in Europe and Asia, over conditions at the mine.
Nippon Mining and Metals Co, Japan's largest copper smelter, said on Thursday that a June copper delivery from Ok Tedi had been delayed.
Hriehwazi said the mine had not found it necessary to purchase concentrates from outside sources to meet its supply commitments despite the delays.
Scheduled maintenance work on one of the mine's two ore grinding mills, brought forward due to the drought, has started and is expected to take about a week to complete, Hriehwazi said.
Some employees have been asked to use up accrued leave while others are enrolling in training programmes as alternatives to mine work.
BHP normally ships by barge about 50,000 tonnes of concentrate a month from the mine to a ship-loading silo vessel at the mouth of the Fly River, but the river level is now too low for the barges.
A storehouse of concentrates at the silo vessel have run dry, BHP said last week.
Ok Tedi is 52.6 percent owned by BHP. Canada's Inmet Mining Corp owns 17.4 percent and the rest is held by the Papua New Guinea government.
